summary: CLM-000826 shows several elevated risk signals relative to home-policy baselines: reporting was delayed 52 days versus a homeowners policy requirement of 24-hour notification and a baseline average of under 6 days, the claimant has 5 previous claims versus a baseline average of 2.62, and the claimed amount ($22,000, 44% of policy limit) is well above both the baseline average claim size and the estimated loss value of $13,439. The claim record's own fraud indicator flags corroborate multiple_claims, inconsistent_narrative, and delayed_reporting. No overlapping vendor, contact, or policy connections were found linking this claim to a broader staged-claim ring, so this appears to be an isolated case warranting deeper documentation review rather than evidence of an organized scheme.
red_flags_identified: Delayed reporting: 52 days versus homeowners policy's 24-hour notification requirement and a dataset baseline average of ~5.9 days
Elevated prior claim frequency: 5 previous claims versus a home-policy baseline average of 2.62
Claim amount ($22,000) is roughly double the home-policy baseline average claim ($10,627) and is an outlier relative to the baseline standard deviation
Claim-to-limit ratio of 44% far exceeds the baseline average of 16%
Claim amount ($22,000) diverges notably from the estimated loss value ($13,439), a ~64% overstatement
Claim record's own fraud_indicators field explicitly flags multiple_claims, inconsistent_narrative, and delayed_reporting
